learn.title: How it works
learn.p.title: P first, then S
learn.p.body: A quake sends out two kinds of waves. P waves are fast and gentle. S waves are slower and do most of the damage. Early warning works because an alert can travel faster than the S wave.
learn.depth.title: Depth widens the blind zone
learn.depth.body: Straight above a deep quake the waves still need seconds to reach the surface, and an alert needs more seconds to be sent. People close to the epicenter feel the S wave before the alert, or with it.
learn.mmi.title: What MMI means
learn.mmi.body: Modified Mercalli Intensity describes what people felt and what broke, from I (not felt) to X and above (extreme). It is not the magnitude, and it changes from place to place.
learn.real.title: What is real and what is modelled
learn.real.body: Real: where, when and how deep the quake was, the arrival times analysts picked, the strong motion instruments, the felt reports and the ShakeMap, all from USGS. Modelled: where the P and S fronts are, from the iasp91 Earth model. Surface waves and local ground are not modelled. Strong motion instruments and felt reports appear when the modelled S front reaches them, but what they show was measured or reported.
learn.sources: Sources: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program, ObsPy TauP (iasp91), OpenStreetMap contributors, OpenFreeMap, Natural Earth, EarthScope.
